artworks.title: The Embassy to Achilles (Attic red-figure hydria, Munich)
artworks.description: Munich hydria: Phoenix and Odysseus stand before sulking Achilles — Iliad 9 made visible, the foster-father's Meleager parable still to fail.

artworks.title: The Embassy to Achilles (Attic red-figure cup, Louvre G146)
artworks.description: Louvre G146 names the ambassadors: Phoenix, Ajax, and Odysseus before Achilles in his hut — persuasion, pride, and the cost of wrath in three registers.

artworks.title: Achilles Receiving the Ambassadors of Agamemnon
artworks.description: Ingres' Prix de Rome canvas: Odysseus speaks while Phoenix and Ajax attend Achilles and Patroclus — neoclassical calm for the embassy that cannot bend the hero.

popCulture.title: Iliad
popCulture.description: Book IX — Odysseus, Ajax, and Phoenix fail to bend Achilles' wrath — remains epic's great scene of refused persuasion.

popCulture.title: Achilles
popCulture.description: The hero who will not return for gifts — only for Patroclus' death — the embassy defines his stubborn honor.
